findings: Server serializes cancelled subscriptions with status value "canceled" (US spelling, single L), but the documented contract's enum only contains "cancelled" (UK spelling, double L) — the server's own output is not a member of its documented enum.

Client's isCancelled() checks sub.status === "cancelled" (UK spelling) while the server only ever emits "canceled" (US spelling) for cancelled subscriptions, so the comparison always evaluates false — this exactly reproduces the reported bug of the cancelled banner never appearing.

Server returns amount: sub.amountCents (a cents value) while the documented contract specifies amount is in dollars; client's formatAmount() does `$${sub.amount.toFixed(2)}` assuming sub.amount is already dollars, so displayed amounts will be rendered 100x too large.

Both serialize() and isCancelled()/formatAmount() carry inline comments asserting spec compliance ("US spelling", "UK spelling, matches the documented contract", "assumes dollars, per the documented contract") even though the server and the documented contract actually disagree on both the status string and the amount unit — the comments assert correctness that the code does not have.

In the non-cancelled branch, serialize() passes sub.status straight through unvalidated/untransformed instead of normalizing it against the documented enum, so any value the underlying data model produces beyond "active"/"paused" would reach the client unchecked.
